competencies.text: Differentiate translational motion from rotational motion.
Relate linear quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration) to angular quantities (angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration).

days.title: Translational vs Rotational Motion
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to differentiate translational motion from rotational motion and describe how linear and angular quantities relate to each other.

🔍 Two Ways Things Move

In physics, motion can be classified into two broad categories:

TypeDescriptionEveryday Examples
Translational motionAn object moves from one point to another without rotating. Every part moves the same distance in the same direction.Walking in a straight line, a car driving forward, a ball rolling down a ramp, an elevator going up
Rotational motionAn object spins around a fixed axis. Different parts of the object move at different speeds depending on their distance from the axis.Ceiling fan blades, bicycle wheels, spinning top, Earth's rotation, hands of a clock

🔗 Linear vs Angular Quantities

Both types of motion share similar measurements, just in different units:

Linear (Translational)Angular (Rotational)Relationship
Displacement (d) — meters (m)Angular displacement (θ) — radians (rad)d = r × θ
Velocity (v) — m/sAngular velocity (ω) — rad/sv = r × ω
Acceleration (a) — m/s²Angular acceleration (α) — rad/s²a = r × α

Where r = radius (distance from the axis of rotation).

⚙️ Key Insight

For a rotating object, the farther a point is from the axis, the faster it moves — because it has to cover a bigger circle in the same amount of time. This is why:

  • The outer edge of a fan blade moves faster than the center.
  • The tip of a windmill blade moves faster than the base.
  • On a Ferris wheel, riders at the rim feel faster than riders near the center.

💡 Real-Life Applications

  • Sports: A golfer swings a club — the longer the club, the faster the clubhead moves.
  • Vehicles: Wheels convert rotational motion into translational motion (the car moves).
  • Machines: Gears, pulleys, and belts transfer and change rotational motion.
  • Astronomy: Earth both revolves around the Sun (translational) and rotates on its axis (rotational).

📌 Quick Check

  • Is a rolling ball translational, rotational, or both?
  • Why does the tip of a long propeller blade move faster than the hub?
  • If a wheel of radius 0.5 m rotates with angular velocity 4 rad/s, what is its linear velocity? (Answer: v = r × ω = 2 m/s)

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Motion in Real Life
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best physics-based reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🚴 You notice that the outer edge of a bicycle wheel moves faster than the hub (center) even though they rotate together. Which best explains this?

choices.label: A) The outer edge is made of lighter material.
B) Points farther from the axis have greater linear velocity (v = r × ω).
C) The hub has more mass.
D) The wheel has less friction at the center.

scenario.text: ⚽ A football rolls across the field without slipping. What type of motion does the ball exhibit?

choices.label: C) Both translational and rotational motion

scenario.text: 🌀 A washing machine drum spins at 1200 rpm. Which quantity best describes how fast the drum is spinning?
🏀 A basketball player spins a ball on her finger. The ball rotates but its center stays in place. What kind of motion is the center experiencing?
🌍 Earth moves around the Sun while also spinning on its own axis. Which statement is TRUE?

choices.label: A) Earth's orbit around the Sun is translational; its spin on its axis is rotational.
D) Earth does not move; the Sun orbits Earth.
